A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for symmetric and almost symmetric triangulations, the finite volume element method for the homogeneous heat problem has optimal error estimates for initial values only in L2.
, in contrast to finite difference methods, the finite volume element method does not lead to an optimal error estimate for initial data only from L2, unless the mesh has a very specific symmetry.

, in the semidiscrete setting, the error estimates are of optimal second order, provided the initial data are sufficiently regular, and that the error estimates are first order for initial data that are only in L2, unless the triangulation is symmetric.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lumped mass approach is not the only one for which error estimates for smooth or nonsmooth initial conditions are optimal.
the finite volume element method is more robust than the lumped mass finite element method with respect to nonsymmetric triangulations, which are frequently encountered in practice.
, for nonsmooth initial conditions, a symmetric finite volume method is not necessarily superior to the lumped mass scheme.
